messages:
alex_peopleops: Heads-up — we have a conversion edge-case I need help with. Contractor Diego (diego_engineer) converted to full-time on 2025-10-03 but was paid twice in Oct: final contractor invoice (1099) in USD and first payroll run (W-2) in EUR after relocation. Withholdings look off and benefits need retro enrollment. Can payroll + tax advise on next steps?

sam_payroll: Thanks Alex. Can you paste payroll IDs and the two payline references? we need payrun IDs + gross amounts + currencies to start.

alex_peopleops: Sure — contractor invoice ID `INV-2025-1098-DG` gross USD 9,200. First salary payrun ID `PR-2025-10-08-FT-DG` gross EUR 5,100 (pro-rated). Diego relocated to IE (Ireland) on 2025-10-01 and elected Irish tax residency.

sam_payroll: Note: our system generated a 1099 for the contractor run (US entity) and W-2 processing for EU payroll. That mismatch will trigger duplicate reporting. Paging Lina from tax. @lina_tax — can Ireland residency change retro to 10/1 affect the 1099 vs W-2 filing?

lina_tax: Short answer: yes. If Diego was resident in Ireland on the payroll date and services after conversion are employment, the US 1099 might be incorrect for EU-sourced wages. We need to determine which services were performed when, and whether the contractor work was performed physically outside the US. Also need to check tax treaty for dual residence.

diego_engineer: I was onsite in SF for the final contractor week (9/29–10/2) and then flew to Dublin on 10/3 morning. The invoice covers work through 10/2. My FT contract started on 10/3 and all salary days were in EU.

marie_finance: Sounds like the contractor invoice legitimately covers pre-relocation work (USD). We still need to ensure correct withholding for the W-2 earnings (Irish payroll) and avoid double US reporting. Two possible fixes: (1) reclassify the 1099 to payroll and issue a corrected 1099/1099-Cancellation + W-2; or (2) leave 1099 but add explanatory docs and coordinate with tax. Lina — what's cleaner for multi-country compliance?

lina_tax: Cleaner is to treat the contractor invoice as contractor income for US-sourced work (if performed in US) and ensure W-2 only for employment income after conversion. Because invoice covers up to 10/2 and physical presence was in US, leaving the 1099 is defensible. But we must ensure we don't gross-up or withhold US taxes on the W-2 for the same days. We also need to confirm payroll withholding for Irish PAYE on the W-2 earnings and issue Form 1099 only for the USD invoice.

alex_peopleops: Ok — actionable items?

sam_payroll: I'll do the following: 1) Confirm what tax jurisdiction was used when generating the 1099 (payroll system record). 2) Confirm whether any US federal/state withholding was applied to the W-2 run by mistake. 3) If duplicates flagged, generate 1099-C or W-2c process notes. I'll update in this thread.

payroll_bot: Automated check complete — 1099 issued under US entity (EIN: 12-3456789) for INV-2025-1098-DG. W-2 issued under EU payroll umbrella (Ireland) for PR-2025-10-08-FT-DG. No US withholding applied on W-2.

sam_payroll: Received. Next: Marie, we need to ensure benefits enrollment is backdated to FT start 2025-10-03. People Ops to confirm effective date and benefits vendor to accept retro enrollment. Also Diego needs enrollment windows for PTO/care.

marie_finance: I'll coordinate benefits billing adjustments and confirm whether premiums for Oct should be employer-paid for pro-rated period. Also will check accounting entries for forex differences on the two runs.

alex_peopleops: Diego — HR note: we'll enroll you retro to 10/3. Expect benefits confirmation email tomorrow and confirm your Irish address for payroll citizenship/residency docs. Lina, any doc requests to support our position on the 1099?

lina_tax: Yes — please provide: (1) travel itinerary showing in-US dates through 10/2; (2) signed contractor statement for the invoice confirming work location; (3) copy of offer letter showing FT start date 10/3. That should substantiate leaving 1099 as-is. If any of those are missing we should consider reclassification.

diego_engineer: Uploaded travel receipts + flight itinerary to the thread link: https://files.redwood/payroll/diogo/relocation — also attached signed contractor invoice PDF.

sam_payroll: Got them. I'll log a ticket with payroll ops to flag the payruns and mark as "contractor-final" vs "FT-start" and run a manual audit. Ticket #PAY-4521.

alex_peopleops: Thanks all. Please post updates here when ticket moves or if payroll/tax needs more docs. If we need to issue any corrected tax forms (1099c or W-2c) let's coordinate timing before year-end filings. :thumbsup:
